category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: Unsure which local tenancy law applies
expected: Identifies Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 alongside general Transfer of Property Act principles.
prompt: I rented a flat in Pune, Maharashtra. Which tenancy law applies to my deposit dispute?
raw_response:
I am very sorry to hear about your security deposit dispute, but I am here to help guide you through your rights under Indian law.

### | Your Situation
You rented a residential flat in Pune, Maharashtra, and are now facing a dispute regarding your security deposit refund. The core issue involves determining the applicable legal framework to claim your rightful money back from the landlord.

### | Your Legal Position
- **Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999**: This primary state enactment governs tenancy matters in Pune, Maharashtra, ensuring that landlords cannot make arbitrary, unlawful deductions from your rightful dues.
- **Model Tenancy Act, 2021 & State Guidelines**: While modern guidelines recommend a maximum security deposit cap of two months' rent for residential premises, Section 13 mandates the full refund of your security deposit upon vacating, subject only to valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
- **Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Section 108(m) & (o))**: This provision protects tenants by clarifying that you are not liable for property degradation caused by reasonable wear and tear. Your landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting or natural aging without an explicit contractual basis.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your signed tenancy agreement, payment receipts for the security deposit, bank statements, handover inspection photos, and all written chat or email communications with your landlord.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your landlord clearly stating the exact deposit amount withheld and granting 15 days to process the full refund.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to comply within the notice period, you can approach the appropriate Rent Authority or Small Causes Court established under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act for dispute resolution.

### Information I still need from you
1. What is the exact amount of the security deposit your landlord is withholding, and how many months of rent did it represent?
2. Did you have a written and registered leave and license agreement, and what specific reason did the landlord give for withholding your deposit?

citations.title: Relief against forfeiture and prohibition against cutting off essential supplies
citations.description: No landlord shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service (water, electricity, lifts) enjoyed by the tenant. Violation is punishable with imprisonment or fine.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.
